# GmpDivisionByKnownZero

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Use a nonzero GMP divisor.

## Example

```php{2}
<?php
$n = gmp_div_q('23', '0');
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 2: Use a nonzero GMP divisor.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- gmp_div_q, gmp_div_r, gmp_div_qr or gmp_mod has an integer zero or valid zero-valued integer string divisor. Include proven gmp_init zero values; exclude ambiguous bases and unknown operands.
- Resolve builtin functions, extension classes, constants and method receivers, including aliases and supported named arguments. Inspect reachable operations in one lexical scope with bounded local flow.
- Emit one finding per violating operation. Never infer policy from names or comments. When the proof is inconclusive, nothing is reported.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Exclude shadowed or unresolved symbols, incomplete code, unknown required constants, ambiguous receiver identity and unsupported versions. Reassignment, escaping aliases, and unknown calls invalidate dependent flow facts.
- A divisor that reads a local variable is not a known zero when that local cannot be trusted. That local is proven only while nothing in its scope can change it behind its plain assignments, anywhere and in any statement order: `++` or `--` on it or on one of its elements; a `catch`, `foreach` key or value binding it; a reference to it (a by-reference assignment on either side, a by-reference `foreach` over it, a by-reference array item, a by-reference capture by a nested closure, or an argument, other than the inspected argument itself, that a resolved callee binds by reference or that a callee custos cannot resolve receives); a write naming its target at run time (a variable variable, `extract()`, one-argument `parse_str()` or `mb_parse_str()`, `include`/`require`, `eval`); or a `$GLOBALS` access other than a literal entry naming another variable. A `global` or `static` declaration of it, or a by-reference capture by the closure that is the scope, removes the proof too. In top-level code, where locals are globals, a `global` declaration naming it in any function of the file, or a `$GLOBALS` access anywhere in the file, does as well. The same holds for every local whose value an assignment stores into it, whatever the assigned expression computes, directly or through further assignments. A read inside an arrow function also checks the scopes the arrow function captures from. A counter initialized to zero and incremented in a loop is ordinary code.
- Both @custos-ignore GmpDivisionByKnownZero and @noinspection GmpDivisionByKnownZero suppress this native rule.

## Fix

None. A safe repair requires choosing values, error handling, or application behavior.

## PHP versions

Apply throughout PHP 5.3–8.5 only where the extension API and syntax exist.  Do not flag API unavailability through this rule.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "GmpDivisionByKnownZero": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore GmpDivisionByKnownZero
```
